 New MLS salary rankings: Messi takes nearly half of Inter Miami’s entire $59.37M payroll as four stars join him in league’s elite $10M club

 Edited by Soror Shaiza / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Nov 20, 2026, 17:24 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small

 Print Oct 10, 2026; Miami, Florida, USA; Inter Miami CF forward Leo Messi (10) celebrates after scoring against the D.C. United during the second half at Nu Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images TPX IMAGES OF THE DAY Lionel Messi continues to lead Major League Soccer's salary rankings, with the Inter Miami forward earning more than $28 million in guaranteed compensation. The latest figures also show how the league's highest salaries are expanding, with Robert Lewandowski, Antoine Griezmann, Son Heung-Min and Breel Embolo joining Messi in the group earning more than $10 million. Across MLS, 150 players now receive at least $1 million in guaranteed compensation. Lionel Messi leads MLS salaries ahead of Robert Lewandowski and Antoine Griezmann
 Messi's guaranteed compensation stands at $28.33 million, unchanged from the previous spring salary release but significantly higher than the $20.45 million recorded a year earlier. The Argentine remains comfortably ahead of the rest of the league, with his Inter Miami contract making him MLS's highest-paid player. According to figures published by the MLS Players Association and reported by ESPN , four other players have joined Messi above the $10 million threshold. Chicago Fire forward Robert Lewandowski ranks second with guaranteed compensation of $19.51 million, followed by Orlando City striker Antoine Griezmann on $13.94 million. LAFC's Son Heung-Min earns $11.25 million, while Atlanta United forward Breel Embolo completes the five-player group with $10.81 million. The figures place five of MLS's biggest names in a salary bracket that previously had fewer representatives. All figures are as of October 9, 2026. Salaries for players who arrived during the summer transfer window have been annualised. Messi's guaranteed compensation does not represent his entire earnings from football and commercial arrangements. His wider income has been estimated at approximately $80 million annually, although that figure includes revenue beyond his MLS playing salary. Inter Miami lead MLS team spending as Philadelphia Union sit at the bottom
 Inter Miami's investment in their squad is reflected in a league-high total payroll of $59.37 million. Chicago Fire rank second at $41.29 million, followed by Atlanta United, LA Galaxy and LAFC, each with payrolls exceeding $32 million. The gap between Miami and the rest of the league is considerable, with the club spending more than twice as much as 25 of the other 29 teams. Despite that outlay, Inter Miami finished second in the Eastern Conference during the regular season, behind Supporters' Shield winners Nashville SC, whose payroll was considerably lower at $24.97 million. At the other end of the spending table, Philadelphia Union had the league's lowest payroll at $12.64 million. Sporting Kansas City followed at $13.30 million, ahead of D.C. United ($14.55 million), CF Montreal ($15.02 million) and FC Dallas ($15.49 million). Philadelphia Union's 17-year-old phenom Cavan Sullivan earned $614,000 in guaranteed compensation, the highest ever for an MLS Homegrown player, yet still below the league average ($746,936) and roughly 2% of Lionel Messi's $28.33 million salary, highlighting the stark wage gap between domestic rising stars and imported global icons. MLS average salary rises 18 per cent as 150 players earn at least $1 million
 The increase in spending at the top of the salary table has accompanied broader growth across the league. Average guaranteed compensation for the MLS player pool reached $746,936, an 18 per cent rise from $632,809 in October 2025. Join conversation

 The median guaranteed compensation increased by a more modest 6.4 per cent, reaching $360,042 from $338,347 over the same period. The distinction between the average and median figures reflects the influence of the league's highest earners, whose salaries pull the overall average considerably higher. A total of 150 players now earn at least $1 million in guaranteed compensation, although the average figure includes pool players and retired players who are still owed money. The latest figures therefore cover a wider group than just the active first-team players appearing regularly in MLS matches. The league and the MLS Players Association are currently in the sixth year of their collective bargaining agreement, signed in February 2021. The existing agreement runs until the end of 2027.
